requirement:
When loading a supported legacy evidence record that did not capture its
procedure version, Habeas represents that missing version as `*`.
In-place conversion preserves this wildcard rather than assigning the current
version. The wildcard matches any
requested review revision under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.procedure_match`.
The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application
freshness checks still match. Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set,
input, determination, citation, and site checks intact.

For new assessments, Habeas's validation value supplies a concrete review revision
other than `*`, and the assessment records it.
rationale:
I judged the tests against the text of `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.legacy_freshness`. I read only the supplied test sources and requested no implementation source. The tests cover every obligation in the requirement.

**Missing version loads as `*`**
- `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` decodes legacy records for definition, citation and site subjects. It asserts `record.revision == "*"` and that the output equals the historical record. It also asserts that encoding writes `review_version` as `*`.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once]` loads legacy records through `load_evidence` for all four review kinds. It asserts the loaded revision is `*`.

**In-place conversion keeps `*` and does not assign the current version**
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[current_legacy_authoring_converts_without_configuration_and_stdout_never_converts]` converts a current legacy file with `EvidenceOutput::File`. It asserts `review_version == "*"` and that `view(new) == old`.
- The same test checks that stdout output neither converts nor changes the file.

**`*` matches any requested revision, while concrete versions still compare exactly**
- `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields]` asserts that a `*` record is current for a requested revision of `future-review-version`. It asserts that a record with revision `old-concrete-version` is not current for `REVIEW_VERSION`. It asserts that a `*` record is not current once the input text changes, even with the request `any`.

**The record is current when inputs and application checks match, and version matching leaves every other check intact**
- In `every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once`, the unchanged legacy `*` record produces no findings for each kind. Native `*` and native `REVIEW_VERSION` encodings produce the same findings.
- Each semantic mutation is applied to a `*` record, and the test asserts a specific finding for it:
  - determination false;
  - a changed input hash or text;
  - changed subject text;
  - a changed reference-set hash;
  - citation file, item and commentary;
  - site requirement, file and item;
  - site queries and fixmes;
  - `applies` false.
- The native conversion of each mutated record is asserted to produce the same findings as the legacy file.
- Staleness loads successfully (`is_some()`) and is reported as a finding.
- Malformed fields, an unsupported format version and a bad `review_version` header are rejected on load, and the file stays unchanged.

**New assessments record a concrete version other than `*`**
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version]` asserts the assessment value's `review_version` equals `REVIEW_VERSION` and is not `*`. It also decodes the record and checks that its dependencies include the input fingerprint.

No obligation is untested, and no assertion contradicts the requirement. Matching of only the complete `*` and of the selected criterion is the cited `procedure_match` requirement's own scope. The tests still exercise exact comparison of concrete versions. No acknowledgments (`{fixme}`) apply.

The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application

For new assessments, Habeas's validation value supplies a concrete review revision

The revision matches when the stored `Record::revision` is `*` or equals the
requested revision exactly. Only the complete stored value `*` is a wildcard;
other values compare literally. A wildcard leaves dependency comparison and
result decoding unchanged. It matches revisions for the selected source and
criterion only, and does not supply evidence for other criteria.
